obligations.note: release() now returns the stored release only when it is less than one day old. A replay of the same instruction_id a day or more later skips the idempotency return and calls _send_disbursement again, so a second disbursement is sent. The function's own docstring still says a repeat release returns the first release.

Ledger entry ACR-0403 (PAY-2 trace, covering payments.py#release at e5bf646) has lapsed because release changed in behaviour. The only replacement is the sample test test_sampled_release_is_idempotent, and its JUnit report is not credibly from this change's CI run (see CHG-4).
Ticket CHG-26088 is standard and approved by change manager Erik Brandt at 2026-10-16T06:20Z, before the change was opened. Its component payments.payments covers the only touched file, payments.py.
The code_review approval is from sofia.santos@fernbrook.example, who holds change_approver for payments and is a different person from the author Mara Costa.
The approval names head commit cfa8da2, which is the only commit on the change.

run.json reports success on head cfa8da2 on ci-runner-06, started 2026-10-16. The attached JUnit report, however, is timestamped 2026-10-23 (after the 2026-10-19 review time) and was produced on host dev-laptop-7.local, so it cannot be confirmed as this run's output.

summary: The change makes release idempotency time-limited: an instruction replayed one day or more after its first release is sent to core banking again. That directly violates PAY-2, and no exception in the register covers it. The test evidence is also inconsistent: the JUnit report postdates the review time and comes from a workstation rather than the CI runner, so the lapsed PAY-2 evidence has not been credibly replaced. Ticket and approval records are otherwise in order, but the PAY-2 violation alone requires rejection.
